contracts.rule: engines are spawned by path, never imported; engines do not import experiments
the matched Metronome baseline and Conveyor use the same worker observation producer; upstream vanilla Metronome remains a reference target

the abstract generated-token count is distinct from gateway delivery; output_token_cap is selected per model by shared workload configuration and must agree across worker, gateway, manifest and matched systems; current first-party workers use it without surplus for every audio segment and stream-end flush, matching the per-period delivery budget; ignore_eos=True does not make the cap a minimum delivery requirement; initial-context preparation uses a separate one-token cap; audio encoding length remains input-dependent; historical unequal-cap runs must be rerun for matched comparisons

runner-specific validation checks service/client/session health, initialization, required observations and delivery syntax; output-cap checks differ between runners, and generic artifact finalization is not full manifest semantic validation; output below the cap is diagnostic; successful execution, exercised mechanisms and paper SLO acceptance are separate judgments

initial-context evidence requires every requested prefill to complete before periodic releases, excludes initialization output from later delivery, releases the automatic-eviction hold without evicting at the barrier, and rejects initialization timeout logs

design requirement: eviction preserves reference history and requires safe execution and transfer references; historical source-audit details are in docs/findings.md#implementation-audit-boundaries and must be rechecked before code changes

activity, physical allocation, valid content, confirmed host coverage, bidirectional transfer state and shared references are separate dimensions; allocation or a store cursor does not establish copy completion; block pools, transfer events and runtime references determine state; design interface: transfer submission, successful transfer completion, publication of valid KV and session readiness are distinct; late or duplicate events must not update unrelated or reused state

the pinned client uses non-namespaced /tmp shard files and shared ports, so runs must not overlap; managed workflow deletes stale shard and aggregate files, requires every expected shard plus the controller to recreate results, and cleans temporary files on exit

design requirement: allocation precedes H2D; computation reads only completed valid KV; capacity deferral, demand overtaking, cancellation and later eviction require coordinated recovery; semantic recovery does not guarantee the deadline
formal evidence is clean; dirty diagnostic evidence carries a reconstructable patch artifact

current prototype, measured path, model/modality, output architecture, hardware, topology, and experiment profile do not define paper scope until the paper contract and experiment matrix are explicitly frozen

design convention: the next planned tick is the current period soft deadline; c-r is deadline latency, c-a is diagnostic, and delayed submission does not shift the deadline; fixed network delay is a provisional analysis assumption

Implementation: MaximumContextPlanner charges the live backend maximum context and complete destination intervals without growth prediction or horizon renewal; conservative calibrated costs, stable phases and fixed ceilings. Open-loop frontend checks retained input plus generation before backend enqueue; no truncation to continue. Cost calibration and measured capacity remain separate from CPU feasibility tests.

analysis requirement, not measured capacity: time-aligned training motivates small typical generation per update but does not impose a hard token cap; compute slack must be established for all admitted sessions at the full-residency capacity boundary and must cover phase-dependent batching costs, transfer interference and scheduling delays; a maximum-context projection may derive each device's batch from its memory ceiling and estimate batched prefill/decode with explicit efficiency and KV-reuse assumptions, but its remaining budget is not measured idle time or a complete-pipeline guarantee, and weights shared across a batch do not imply shared session KV; assumed efficiencies must be distinguished from calibration, retain adverse sensitivity cases, and recompute dependent tables and external comparisons when assumptions change; period times effective restoration bandwidth bounds restored bytes per period, while peak memory savings also depend on actual release-to-preallocation intervals; full eviction is infeasible when total restoration exceeds this budget or individual time-and-space constraints, not universally

design requirement, not implementation status: phase assignment spreads restoration demand across the period to extend useful H2D link activity, support more KV restoration and eviction per cycle, and expand effective KV capacity through GPU space reuse; transfer overlap with computation in other sessions is not the capacity mechanism; the planner selects the residency arrangement and the session manager controls its runtime H2D scheduling; restoration needs both a scheduled transfer window and sufficient space for full destination preallocation; per-session eviction amounts share memory, transfer and compute budgets; uniform slots do not prove admission feasibility; session groups are scheduling objects, and a group schedule retains per-session history and per-block safety conditions without requiring an atomic group transfer; selected execution policy: allocate each session restoration destination in full, count every complete queued or in-flight destination immediately, preserve planned allocation and copy order without partial destination holding or allocation bypass, and publish per-session readiness without a group execution barrier; the current managed path implements complete per-session allocation, stable ordering and versioned H2D-drained transitions; unit tests cover reference lifetime and no allocation bypass, while measured capacity remains a separate evidence obligation; design boundary: session groups organize residency scheduling, while the inference backend owns execution scheduling and model computation, including batching when used; continuous batching is not a required backend policy; backend replacement requires compatible execution-event and KV-state operations and is not a claim of existing multi-backend support; proactive cyclic KV recomputation is reserved for future work as a planner decision extension, with replay-capable backend execution and joint resource feasibility required before claiming support

Implemented conservative membership changes pause new H2D allocation, wait for allocated H2D to settle, recheck current physical allocation under the adapter lock and publish a monotonically versioned plan. Existing phases and ceilings are unchanged; arbitrary budget/phase replacement remains unsupported. Departure reserves credit until request and copy cleanup complete.

Open-loop replay preserves immutable source samples, fractional arrival phases and original deadlines. Reject infeasible arrivals once, distinguish a pending plan transition from rejection, and never expose future departures to the planner. Report offered/admitted/rejected and on-time/late/unfinished model work, original-source delay, alignment and planned/actual sends. Dynamic and fixed schedules hash recorded audio and keep input and arrival randomness separate; the legacy post-admission cohort client is a separate diagnostic path.

KV L/R slices measure scheduler-observed windows, not DMA time; demand ends at waiting-request promotion and prefetch at completion handling. Logical KV bytes may be derived only from the run manifest geometry; physical transfer bandwidth requires correlated copy events and actual copy bytes. An unmatched L means completion was not observed, not proof that DMA failed. Manager prefetch completion is recorded by the independent copy callback. CUPTI GPU activity durations remain separate from CPU windows and CUDA stream-event intervals; correlated physical payload bytes must match submission bytes.

The opt-in manager executes supplied per-session plans independently of model steps. Eviction selects complete confirmed-host-backed blocks with no competing GPU references. Idle retained blocks, host sources and in-flight destinations remain pinned; incomplete destinations are not published. Scheduler/pool mutation is locked, model execution is not. The adapter rejects async scheduling, multiple KV groups, speculative decoding and worker-side KV zeroing. No joint admission solver or deadline guarantee is implied.

Default first-party audio preprocessing preserves valid mel features, mask lengths and audio token IDs while limiting padding to the actual resampled input plus the centered STFT right boundary, rounded to a hop. Keep original model-limit truncation; do not crop to the nominal period or mutate a shared processor. Explicit max_length, normalization and dither retain upstream behavior.

Legacy diagnostic implementation; not the current maximum-context planning/open-loop evaluation contract. Implemented conservative candidate policy: existing phases and eviction budgets stay fixed; a free slot is insufficient; explicit finite-horizon compute, bidirectional copy, full-destination GPU allocation, host capacity and growth estimates must pass before admission. Profile calibration and general joint optimization remain separate work. Reviews publish risk, not lifetime guarantees. Runtime memory-saving credit is capped by confirmed recoverable non-shared backing; new sessions get no speculative credit, while transfer service still reserves the maximum future restoration budget.

Legacy cohorts queue before playback; open-loop cohorts preserve source time and reject infeasible arrivals once. session.end drains final input and capped output; completion needs final frontend output and backend request/copy cleanup. Closing retains admission credit, duplicate/late operations cannot resurrect identity, and readiness pins survive until execution references are acquired.

Legacy finite cohort diagnostic only: Every offered manifest identity must complete exactly once; sending audio, socket disconnect and RPC return are not completion. Admission waiting and post-admission audio time remain distinct. Synthetic inputs are labelled. Per-cycle SLO uses the independent input-identity/completion collector. Fixed-cap drain does not establish arbitrary variable-length model support.

A slot is a multi-session group. The sum of member eviction ceilings must fit its shared restore window, including overhead and safety. Actual safe eviction grows up to each ceiling; short histories cannot justify overcommitting future transfer capacity. Retained growth remains charged to GPU.

Legacy diagnostic SLO checker; not the current simplified evaluation protocol. Fixed sample-count input identities cross release/receive/ingest/compute completion. Deadlines use the frozen source sample-availability clock and earliest eligible planned tick plus period, never actual late arrival or submission. All N sessions start behind an admission barrier; uncompleted/unsubmitted inputs remain in denominator. Invalid measurement cannot establish a capacity boundary.

Coalescing preserves every original physical mapping and only merges adjacent source and destination ranges. Bounded batches share one stream; lifetime and publication remain tied to the final device event. No host synchronization is added by the GIL-preserving submission wrapper.

GPU capture is off or enabled for the entire business run. Start completes before client launch; stop/export runs after client exit and before worker cleanup. No timed mid-run stop. Failed/incomplete export cannot pass validation.

A selected model preset pins checkpoint revision, input adapter and KV geometry together. Runtime allocations/physical transfer bytes come from actual tensors, not the previous model geometry. Fixed-budget audio-input/text-output support does not establish native duplex audio-output integration.

Volume ceilings, actual restore timeliness and whole-input SLO are separate. In-flight copies are never cut off at window end; completed valid KV is required. Report late completion and unassociated transfers explicitly.

The hashed runtime profile pins a consistent CUDA compiler/CRT/NVVM/CCCL family and model revisions. Worker environment exposes the selected venv ninja and wheel-provided CUDA toolkit. Machine checks verify BF16, FlashInfer sampling JIT, complete model shards, physical KV roundtrip and multi-session lifecycle. Functional checks with uncalibrated costs do not establish capacity.

Optional intrusive diagnostics compare all copied physical KV bytes after observed device completion and before publishing or releasing pins; mismatch fails the copy service and retains uncertain references. This synchronizes the GPU and cannot be used for formal performance.

Managed eviction preserves unselected blocks including the unfinished tail. Full restoration must preserve every saved logical block hash and computed-token frontier before pins transfer into the original backend block table. No computation or readiness publication with missing blocks; no suffix recomputation from prefix-cache re-entry. Cancellation retains in-flight references.
